title: YC Summer 2026
method: A company joins a group only if its own YC one-liner contains a phrase that supports it; the rest are judgment calls or stay ungrouped.
overview: All 230 companies in YC Summer 2026. 164 fall into eight groups; the other 66 don't share a clear group and are shown in grey.

groups.name: AI-native service firms
groups.rubric: The company describes itself as the service provider (firm, practice, agency, brokerage, insurer, BPO, clinic) rather than software sold to one.
groups.narration: 24 companies describe themselves as the service firm itself, not software sold to one. Billow, Rational and Last Accounting Company are accounting firms. Florin and Princeps are insurance companies. Peer is a freight brokerage.

groups.name: Agent infrastructure
groups.rubric: Infrastructure whose users are AI agents or the developers running them: gateways, routing, inference, identity, payments, hosting, developer environments.
groups.narration: 27 companies build infrastructure for AI agents: payments, identity, hosting and routing. Agentcard lets agents buy things online. Inkbox provides identity and communication. machine0 describes itself as AWS for agents.

groups.name: Data and evals for AI labs
groups.rubric: Sells training data, evaluations, benchmarks, RL environments or simulations used to train or test AI models.
groups.narration: 24 companies sell data, evaluations or training environments to AI labs. Markov sells expert computer-use data. Petrarch sells internal industrial data. Tokenless finds flaws in RL environments and evals.

groups.name: Defense
groups.rubric: Builds for military, defense, government security or contested environments.
groups.narration: 13 companies build for defense: drone swarms from Earendil and Greypoint, radar from Vernius, exoskeletons from Edgerun, rocket cargo from Hop Aero. Isengard lists 30 people, the largest team in the batch.

groups.name: Robotics
groups.rubric: Builds robots, drones or autonomous physical systems, or the core infrastructure to run them.
groups.narration: 22 companies build robots for specific jobs. Grip handles waste, Salem works in hazardous spaces, and Proprio maintains data centers. Nori lists a humanoid robot at 1,688 dollars.

groups.name: Compute and chips
groups.rubric: Works on compute supply: chips, semiconductors, data centers, compute markets or energy for compute.
groups.narration: 16 companies work on compute: chips, data centers and markets. Computable is building a derivatives exchange for compute. Touchmark is a market for future inference capacity. Atomarine is building floating, nuclear-powered data centers.

groups.name: Vertical operations
groups.rubric: Sells AI that runs the day-to-day operations of one kind of business (an operating system, back office, or AI workforce for a named industry).
groups.narration: 26 companies sell AI that runs the operations of one kind of business: auto shops, hotels, restaurants, wholesale distributors. Bernard, with nine people, builds AI employees for home-appliance repair companies.

groups.name: Bio, chemistry and materials
groups.rubric: Works in biology, medicine development, chemistry, materials or consumer health science.
groups.narration: 12 companies work in biology, chemistry or materials. TareBio is developing vaccines for cancer and infection. Gamgee is working on cancer, starting with dogs. Molagri makes resistance-free pesticides.

items.name: OpenTag

items.name: Conifer
items.summary: Least cost routing system to reduce 70%+ token spend
items.description: There are thousands of models, providers, and harnesses, each with its own pricing and strengths, leaving an overwhelming number of choices when it comes to managing token spend and intelligence. Conifer uses intelligent routing and orchestration logic to handle the full path of each query: model selection, provider choice, and cache management. It all runs inside your existing harness, so tools like Claude Code and Codex work without changing your setup. By centralizing where inference occurs, Conifer lets companies save on their inference bill while leaving teams free to focus on what they are building.

items.name: Experiential Labs
items.summary: Open source AI gateway that turns your traffic into better models
items.description: We are building an open source gateway for AI budget holders to control model access and turn their traffic into better models that they own. We're a team that has earned an ML PhD at Georgia Tech, scaled AutoGPT to 160k GitHub stars, and led a self-driving simulation team at Waabi.

items.name: Edviro
items.summary: AI That Operates Energy Infrastructure
items.description: Edviro builds AI that operates energy infrastructure. We connect to meters, HVAC systems, batteries, solar, and other energy equipment and continuously handle the work required to keep them efficient: detecting and diagnosing problems to forecasting demand, simulating fixes, creating work orders, coordinating maintenance, and controlling equipment where authorized. Our energy world models learn how each site behaves, choose the highest-value actions, and verify the results against real operational, meter, and billing data.

items.name: CoArena
items.summary: The biggest crowdsourced benchmark for Computer-Use
items.description: CoArena is a live arena where anyone can use the world's top computer-use models racing two of them on the same real computer task and judging which one did it better. Every battle becomes something the AI labs can't build themselves, an honest test of their agents on real work, and the data to make them better.

items.name: Caution
items.summary: Hosting platform for software you can't afford to have hacked
items.description: Caution is a hosting platform for software you can't afford to get hacked. It simplifies and extends confidential compute, and lets developers deploy workloads to secure enclaves in minutes and give customers, auditors, and counterparties cryptographic proof that production is running the exact reviewed source code, build, configuration, and runtime - not an opaque binary controlled by a cloud operator or internal admin. Confidential computing hardware exists, but the tooling is too fragmented and incomplete for most teams to use well. Today, attestation often proves only that a binary has a certain hash; it does not prove what source code produced that binary. Building the missing deployment, reproducibility, and verification layer requires specialized security engineering and often locks teams into one cloud or hardware stack. Caution turns that into a simple git-based workflow that builds reproducible enclave images, provisions infrastructure, …

We’ve developed WaveZip, which captures waveforms 500x smaller with 200x less overhead, and Wave, which beats frontier models on industry chip debugging benchmarks. We’re Rishov Sarkar (Georgia Tech Ph.D. in chip simulation) and Athreya Anand (ex-Google, M.S. ML/AI), YC S26. https://hardwareintelligence.ai

items.name: Osseus
items.summary: The frontier data platform for aligned health and biological AI
items.description: In an era of cheap intelligence, the most important application of AI will be to improving human health, globally. Osseus is building the frontier biomedical AI research lab, starting with the clinical datasets, evaluations, and reinforcement learning environments that help AI labs train more capable, aligned, and safe models.

items.name: Allia Health
items.summary: AI-Native Medical Group for Mental Health
items.description: Allia is the first full-stack, AI-native clinical group for mental health. We bring independent practices into one national clinical group that can deliver, measure, and improve care at scale .

items.name: Salem Robotics Inc
items.summary: Deploying robots to replace workers in hazardous spaces
items.description: Our software turns any robot we deploy into an everyday independent worker at your facility. They are able to walk sites, handle instruments, overcome obstacles, collect measurements, and generate auditable compliance records, replacing hours of mandatory manual surveys and inspections. Built by Los Alamos robotics veterans and deterministic-manipulation researchers, we started in nuclear and are already expanding to other hazardous industries.

items.name: Robocurve
items.summary: Evals for robots
items.description: Robocurve builds open-source tools and independent benchmarks to measure how well robots can do real-world jobs. Instead of relying on unverified demo videos from frontier labs, we score their models on reproducible benchmarks that anyone can trust. Today there are no well-run, standardized robotics benchmarks. Labs evaluate in-house, and no independent group has stepped in to run continuous benchmarking as a service. The result is that no one actually knows how good anyone else is, or where the real frontier sits. Good benchmarks require operating and maintaining physical hardware and real-world setups. Simulation only goes so far, since models that look strong in sim can show large performance gaps once deployed in the real world. Building real-world benchmarks means coordinating job-domain experts, evals engineering, and hands-on robotics all at once. Frontier labs are targeting general-purpose robotics by 2028, yet the …

items.name: Autoresearch, Inc.
items.summary: Autoresearch as a service: we solve your hardest measurable problems
items.description: Autoresearch helps teams train agents for tasks where general models are not good enough. Give us a task, your current agent or model, and an evaluation. Autoresearch runs an autoresearch campaign across data, SFT and other post-training methods, continual learning, prompts, tools, harnesses, and systems, then returns the best verified improvement. It runs hosted or in your cloud. We provide the research system around models: persistent memory, full experiment lineage, compute orchestration, and statistical verification. We’re starting with agent and model training, continual learning, and optimization. Reach out to us for early access at founders@autoresearch.inc.

Your team controls what they can access and change, while credentials stay out of the agents’ reach and every call is logged. https://www.onecli.sh

items.name: Vernius Systems, Inc.
items.summary: Mass-deployable radars for air defense
items.description: We make mass-deployable radars for unmanned systems. Our first product is Archimedes, a radar seeker that finds and locks onto targets, enabling autonomous intercept on any drone. We have over $580M in LOIs for Archimedes, across some of the largest defense primes in Ukraine, the EU, and the Middle East. Seekers are the most critical and costly component in every autonomous interceptor. Developing a radar seeker takes a 200+ person team at Raytheon and hundreds of millions of dollars. Archimedes is 100x cheaper than existing radar seekers on the market - and is the first product to make it feasible to deploy radars on every drone.

items.name: Wondering
items.summary: Duolingo for learning anything

You practice, make connections, and form your own insights. Start learning anything for free at https://wondering.app/download

With solar panels made from the Moon, the constraint that limits data center scaling and everything else in space is gone.

items.description: Florin is a full-stack insurance carrier where a model does the underwriting. It then simulates tens of thousands of ways the policy year could go, prices the risk, and returns a bindable quote in under a minute instead of weeks. The team is ex-Google, Tesla, Amazon, and Terrafirma, and the bet is that a carrier built this way wins on loss ratio, speed, and cost at the same time.

Building a company used to mean hiring a building full of people first. With Dock, entrepreneurs can start a real business today and run it like a company of a hundred. You decide where it goes. Your agents make it happen.

items.name: Verdict Machine
items.summary: AI cybersecurity for financial institutions' digital assets
items.description: Verdict Machine uses AI to understand each financial institution's complete on-chain environment, assess its cyber risk and generate tailored controls. The same live model powers transaction prevention, continuous cyber diligence, security posture and cost-efficient wallet screening. Before execution, Verdict Machine evaluates proposed transactions against the institution's active policies. In our first weeks, we started POCs with asset managers and digital-asset infrastructure providers whose systems move billions of dollars every week for financial institutions. We're now in active evaluations with digital-asset teams at some of the world's largest banks. The founding team launched and led blockchain security at Check Point (NASDAQ: CHKP).

items.name: TovenAI
items.summary: AI agents for compliance at institutional trading firms
items.description: TovenAI builds a platform of AI agents that handle manual, data-intensive work for compliance teams at institutional trading firms, with six agents currently live. Our customers range from specialist firms to large global institutions, with our agents supporting multiple compliance workflows at a top-10 institutional brokerage. With prebuilt connectors to more than 30 systems—including Bloomberg, Cloud9, and NICE Actimize—firms can onboard to our platform and evaluate results using their own data in less than a week.

items.name: HyperProbe
items.summary: AI engineer that debugs and fixes production incidents in realtime
items.description: With tools like Cursor and Claude Code, writing software is no longer the bottleneck. Debugging is. Agents cannot fix production crashes using logs and traces that were sized for human eyeballs. The gap is missing data. HyperProbe allows agents to debug live software autonomously. Our SDK drops non-breaking probes straight into running services to read exact variable states from memory at the moment of failure, instead of reasoning backwards from flat logs. Zero redeploys. Under 1% CPU overhead. Automatic PII redaction. We turn 4-hour production war rooms into 10-minute automated resolutions. As agents write and operate more of the world's software, HyperProbe is the runtime observability layer that lets them understand what they built.

items.name: Grip
items.summary: Robots for waste manipulation
items.description: Grip is a robotics company building intelligent robotic systems for waste and recycling. We are starting with organic waste, where removing contaminants from messy, constantly changing streams remains difficult and highly manual. Our technology combines learning-based manipulation and custom hardware to identify and pick objects, learning from real-world operating data, including every successful and failed grasp, to become more reliable and adaptable over time. This helps waste operators reduce manual sorting, recover more valuable material, lower contamination, and deploy automation flexibly across facilities. Over time, Grip aims to expand beyond organics and build the intelligent manipulation layer for trash in general, making waste processing and the circular economy more efficient and scalable.

items.name: Skymerse
items.summary: Autopilot for Flight Operations
items.description: Skymerse is building one AI system for airline flight operations: from planning and monitoring in the operations center to real-time support in the cockpit. It is developing specialized aeronautical models that understand the data, constraints, and procedures behind each flight, replacing fragmented tools and manual interpretation. Notamify, its first product, already serves airline customers and thousands pilots and aviation professionals.

items.name: Hubble
items.summary: AI-native retrieval engine for medical records
items.description: Hubble’s mission is to unify the patient medical record and remove the barriers to accessing it. Today, a person’s health history is scattered across disconnected systems, leaving patients and the people helping them to piece it together. We’re building a future where one authorization unlocks a more complete record, regardless of where someone received care. Our founders previously built healthcare and AI products at Grow Therapy and Amazon One Medical, and we’re backed by Y Combinator, Madrona, and Basis Set. We’re building our team in Seattle, with the opportunity to work directly with the founders and shape how people access and use their health information.

items.name: Shiraz AI

We're starting in contract manufacturing, where lines change every week and both traditional automation and today's VLAs fall over. Our founding team has 20+ years of experience in robotics. Navid was part of the core team that productized Spot at Boston Dynamics and led manipulation projects there. Before that, he was at Rethink Robotics. Mojtaba led whole-body control and manipulation efforts at Amazon Robotics and was a Research Assistant Professor at Northwestern University.

items.name: Mireye
items.summary: Search Engine for the Physical World
items.description: AI agents are starting to act in the real world, but they can't reliably understand it. Every fact about a place has its own silo: land in GIS maps, power in utility portals, people in census tables, policy in county PDFs. All built for humans, none for agents. Underneath, the data is fragmented across thousands of sources, unstructured and complex. Mireye is building the infrastructure that powers agents to make decisions and act in the real world. One API and MCP to connect agents to the physical world with accurate data enrichment, signals and tools. Our mission is to index every inch of the earth, and make it as queryable as the web.

items.name: Tokenless
items.summary: We find flaws in RL environments and evals and help you fix them.
items.description: Tokenless is an applied AI research lab. Our goal is to end reward hacking. We do research and build tools to detect issues with environments and evals, understand model behavior in those environments, and prevent those issues from happening. Correcting them makes training more effective, makes model performance easier to interpret, and is crucial to solving the AI alignment problem. If you’re training models with RL, building environments, or running agent evals, and want more confidence in your environments, we're here to help.

facts.founders: Rohit Agarwal, Andrew Liu, Kev Wang

items.name: Derya
items.summary: AI Brokers for Industrial Trade
items.description: Derya deploys supply chain automations for startups, SMEs, and enterprises that fulfil their entire supply chain function, from prospecting and procurement to distribution of goods. Our mission is to rebuild the supply chain from the ground up, turning one of the world’s hardest coordination problems into an AI native system that moves commodities by being integrated into both the supply chain infrastructure and the customer. We work across robotics, commodities, and food & beverages companies; procuring goods and managing various operation functions for them.

items.name: Pennant
items.summary: The World Model for Corporate Governance
items.description: Led by former institutional proxy voters and technologists with a collective 20+ years of experience, Pennant gives institutional investors, public companies, and corporate advisors voting and governance intelligence to act on their own principles at scale.

items.name: Decawork
items.summary: Training company-specific models that approve AI actions.
items.description: An agent’s access should depend on the task it is doing. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another. Access decisions need to adapt in real time as the agent works, but companies can’t turn every business judgment into a fixed rules or have people manually approve every step. We train small, company-specific models that approve AI actions in real time. They consider the company’s policies and interests, the agent’s current task, and its past actions to decide whether each proposed action should be allowed. Access is specific to the task at hand and reassessed as the agent works. Companies will rent intelligence from AI labs or run open-source models to power their agents. They’ll own the models that keep their entire AI workforce acting in their interests. Decawork is building those models.

items.name: CarSignal
items.summary: The AI Operating System for Auto Shops.
items.description: CarSignal is the AI-native operating system for independent auto repair shops. Most shops still run each repair across disconnected management software, scan tools, parts catalogs, service information, texts, spreadsheets, and knowledge kept in technicians’ heads. That fragmentation slows diagnosis, creates duplicate processes, and leaves customers waiting. CarSignal connects the full repair process in one system. AI agents research vehicle-specific failure patterns and surface the tests that confirm or rule out each cause. The same system carries each job from booking and intake through inspections, estimates, parts, approvals, payment, and follow-up, so technicians spend less time searching and updating systems and more time fixing cars.

items.name: Axelrod

Radiology is already in crisis: there aren't enough radiologists to interpret 1 in 6 medical scans. In 10 years, that gap is growing to 1 in 3 - 246M scans a year. From past experience, we know that point solutions won’t cut it. While there is demand (we have $2.2M in contracts to prove it), bottleneck isn't just software, it's outdated systems and slow, inefficient operations. That's why we own the full stack, clinical and operational, end to end. We met at Carbon Health as we scaled operations 31x and expanded to 100+ clinics. Now we're rebuilding radiology.

items.name: Agnost AI

items.name: ProvenMetal

We automate the bottlenecks - part procurement, DFM review, and assembly - delivering circuit boards in days instead of weeks.

items.name: Gamgee
items.summary: Curing cancer. Starting with dogs.
items.description: ​Gamgee began with Rosie, founder Paul Conyngham’s dog. After surgery, chemotherapy and immunotherapy failed, Rosie was given months to live. Paul used AI and genomic analysis to identify targets in her tumour, then worked with scientists at UNSW to produce what is believed to be the first fully computationally designed mRNA cancer vaccine delivered to a dog. Products like datacenter coolant, GPU thermal paste, paint, and glue are formulations, which are mixtures of around ten ingredients each, and demand for them has grown quickly because of AI and EVs. Designing a new formulation is essentially a search problem, because there are more possible mixtures than anyone could ever test, and none of them can be predicted in advance. As a result, bringing a single formulation to market today takes three to five years of trial and error in a lab. Our models predict how a mixture will behave far faster than the standard methods used today, which lets us design new formulations in weeks rather than years, at a fraction of the cost.
